title: High-Speed Ultraviolet Photoacoustic Microscopy for Histological Imaging with Virtual-Staining assisted by Deep Learning
protocol: Use a Q-switch diode-pumped solid-state laser as an excitation source.
Expand the laser beam using two convex lenses.
Place a pinhole close to the focal point of the first convex lens for spatial filtering.
Reflect the laser beam upward using a 1D galvanometer mirror.
Focus the laser beam using an objective lens and pass it through the center of a ring-shaped ultrasonic transducer before focusing tightly on a sample.
Use a ring-shaped focused ultrasonic transducer to detect ultrasonic waves.
Fix the UT into a lab-made water tank with an optically transparent window at the bottom, covered by a thin quartz coverslip.
Ensure that the active area of the UT is facing upward.
Attach the water tank to a two-axis manual stage for controlling the lateral position of the UT.
Turn on the UV laser and adjust the position of the UT to allow the laser beam to pass through from the center of the UT.
Turn off the UV laser.
Fill the water tank with deionized water to fully immerse the UT.
Connect the output of the UT to two amplifiers with a total gain of 56 dB.
Connect the output of the second amplifier to a data acquisition card (DAQ).
Attach a sample holder to a z-axis manual stage connected to xy-motorized stages.
Place four pieces of double-sided tape surrounding an empty hole in the sample holder.
Attach black tape to a glass slide and place it over the hole, with the black tape facing downward.
Press the glass slide to ensure it is fixed on the sample holder.
Lower the sample holder to immerse the glass slide into water.
Disconnect the ring-shaped UT and amplifiers.
Connect the UT to the pulser/receiver.
Connect the output of the pulser/receiver to an oscilloscope.
Operate the pulser/receiver in Pulse-Echo mode.
Set the pulse amplitude of the pulser/receiver to 6 dB.
Set the gain of the pulser/receiver to 20 dB.
Enable the pulser/receiver.
Adjust the z-position of the sample holder to find the acoustic focal plane with maximum ultrasonic signals.
Change the pulser/receiver mode to transmission and set the gain to 60 dB.
Enable the laser output.
Adjust the z-position of the objective lens to maximize PA signals measured by the oscilloscope.
Adjust the lateral position of the ring-shaped UT to make the generated PA signal symmetric and maximum.
Adjust the z-position of the sample holder to maximize the PA signals.
Repeat steps to optimize both the symmetry and amplitude of the PA signals.
Record the time delay when the PA signals are optimized on the oscilloscope.
Move the sample holder to image different positions of the black tape.
Adjust the sample holder's flatness such that the PA signals have the same time delay as measured previously.
Turn off the laser and connect the UT to the two amplifiers.
Sacrifice a mouse with an overdose of anesthesia.
Harvest the mouse brain following the protocol described in reference18.
Fix the harvested brain in 10% neutral buffered formalin for 24 hours.
Process the fixed brain by dehydration with graded alcohol, clearing with xylene, and embedding with paraffin as described in reference19.
Slice the embedded brain into thin slices (5 µm in thickness) using a microtome.
Place the sample slices on quartz slides.
Dry the slides in an oven at 60 °C for 1 hour.
Deparaffinize the sections using a clearing agent in a fume hood.
Wash the mouse brain with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to remove blood.
Cut a slice of the mouse brain (~5 mm thick).
Wash the brain slice with PBS to remove any remaining blood.
Set the laser repetition rate to 55 kHz.
Set the signal type of the GM driver to triangular.
Set the driving voltage range to ±0.018 V.
Set GMnum to 22.
Set dy to 2.
Set dx to 192.
Adjust the z-axis manual stage to place the sample on the focal plane for obtaining maximum PA signals.
Move both x- and y-axis motors to the desired starting point.
Set the scanning region by setting xn and yn values.
Start the image acquisition program.
Turn off the laser after image acquisition.
Remove the sample holder.
Store the biological samples.
Store fresh biological tissues in 10% neutral buffered formalin.
Stain FFPE mouse brain slices with H&E following the protocol stated in reference 20.
Use collected PA signals to reconstruct the maximum amplitude projection image using a lab-built image processing algorithm.
